record.paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
record.original_question: For every smooth complex projective polarized variety (X,H), does there exist a modified Chern character determined by a class gamma and an upper semicontinuous real function f such that every gamma-tilt-semistable object E satisfies the Bayer-Macri quadratic inequality Qbar_{s,q}(E) >= 0 for all tilt parameters (s,q) above the graph q > f(s)? In dimension 3, such a statement would imply the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on Db(X).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,H)$ be a smooth complex projective polarized variety of dimension $n$. For a class $\gamma\in\bigoplus_{i\ge 2}H^{2i}(X,\mathbb{Q})$, define the twisted Chern character
$$\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}:=(1-\gamma)\cdot\mathrm{ch},$$
and, for real parameters $s,q$, the twisted slope and tilt functions giving rise to the heart $\mathrm{Coh}^{s}(X)$ (the tilt of $\mathrm{Coh}(X)$ at slope $s$ with respect to $H$) and the notion of $\gamma$-tilt-(semi)stability of two-term complexes $E\in\mathrm{Coh}^{s}(X)$. Recall the Bayer–Macrì quadratic form
$$\overline{Q}_{s,q}(E)=(H^{n-1}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{1}(E)-sH^{n}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{0}(E))^{2}-2H^{n}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{0}(E)\cdot(H^{n-2}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{2}(E)-qH^{n}\mathrm{ch}^{\gamma}_{0}(E))\cdot\text{(suitable normalization)},$$
viewed as a quadratic form in the truncated Chern character of $E$ depending on the parameters $(s,q)$ and on $\gamma$.

Question: Does there exist, for every such $(X,H)$, a class $\gamma$ and an upper semicontinuous function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ with the following property? Every $\gamma$-tilt-semistable object $E\in\mathrm{Coh}^{s}(X)$ satisfies
$$\overline{Q}_{s,q}(E)\ \ge\ 0$$
for all pairs $(s,q)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}$ with $q>f(s)$.

In particular, when $\dim X=3$, prove that such $\gamma$ and $f$ exist; deduce that the bounded derived category $D^{b}(X)$ admits Bridgeland stability conditions.
artifact.status_search_result: The original Bayer–Macrì–Toda generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker inequality (the case $\gamma=0$, $f\equiv 0$) is known to fail in general: Schmidt (2016) exhibited a counterexample on the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^3$ at a point. The modified form with a corrective class $\gamma$ and graph $f$ has been verified in several cases (abelian threefolds, Kummer threefolds, Calabi–Yau threefolds of abelian type, and all Fano threefolds via a strengthened Bogomolov-type inequality), yielding Bridgeland stability conditions on $D^{b}(X)$ in those settings. The general statement for arbitrary smooth projective threefolds (and higher dimensions) remains open.

status_evidence.title: Counterexample to the Generalized Bogomolov-Gieseker Inequality for Threefolds
status_evidence.snippet: Schmidt gives a counterexample to the generalized Bogomolov-Gieseker inequality on the blow-up of P^3 at a point.
status_evidence.claim: The naive (untwisted) form of the BMT inequality fails on a smooth projective threefold.

status_evidence.title: Bridgeland Stability Conditions on Fano Threefolds
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on all Fano threefolds is established via a modified Bogomolov-Gieseker type inequality.
status_evidence.claim: A twisted version of the conjecture is known on all Fano threefolds, yielding Bridgeland stability conditions.

status_evidence.title: The space of stability conditions on abelian threefolds, and on some Calabi-Yau threefolds
status_evidence.snippet: Bridgeland stability conditions are constructed on abelian threefolds and certain Calabi-Yau threefolds.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is verified for abelian threefolds and Calabi-Yau threefolds of abelian/Kummer type.
